fact_en: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old, starting right from the Big Bang!
fact_bis: Ang uniberso mga 13.8 ka bilyon ka tuig na ang edad, sukad pa sa Big Bang!
evidence: "Kalibutan" means world/Earth in all 653 corpus body uses (universe is "uniberso", used in 67 of the 85 universe cards), so the headline tells a child the Earth is 13.8 billion years old, contradicting the corpus's own "Yuta 4.5 ka bilyon" cards.

title_tl: 35 km Taas ng Ulap ng Abo
fact_en: Mount Pinatubo's ash cloud rose more than 35 kilometers high into the sky!
fact_bis: Miabot ug kapin sa 35 ka kilometro ang gitas-on sa panganod sa abo nga gibuga sa Pinatubo!
evidence: "Aso" is smoke in Cebuano while ash is "abo" — the body itself says "panganod sa abo", and another card in the corpus exists specifically to teach "Dili Aso ang Panganod" (an ash cloud is not smoke).

fact_en: Johannes Kepler described three laws of planetary motion! These rules explain how planets move in space.
fact_bis: Gihulagway ni Johannes Kepler ang tulo ka balaod sa paglihok sa mga planeta! Nagpasabot kini kung giunsa paglihok sa mga planeta.
evidence: "Bala" is a bullet (the corpus uses "balaod" for law in 171 bodies, including this card's own), so the headline reads "Kepler's Three Bullets".

fact_en: The Sun heats ocean water into vapor that rises, cools in the upper atmosphere, and condenses around tiny dust particles to form clouds.
fact_bis: Gipainit sa adlaw ang tubig sa dagat nga mahimong singaw; misaka kini, nibugnaw sa taas nga atmospera, ug nagkondensa sa palibot sa gagmay nga alikabok aron makahimo ug panganod.
evidence: "Pagtapak" is stepping on/patching, not forming; the body describes condensation forming clouds and the corpus's word for formation is "pagporma", so the headline reads "Stepping on the Cloud".

fact_en: Mayon Volcano in Albay erupts andesite lava, which cools above ground to form hard, dark gray igneous rocks!
fact_bis: Ang Bulkang Mayon sa Albay mo-eruption og andesite lava, nga kung mo-cool sa ibabaw sa yuta maghimo og lig-on, itom-gray nga igneous rocks!
evidence: Last word "Igneo" is cut off; the card itself contains "Igneous".

fact_en: Tectonic plates slowly push until stress overcomes friction, making rocks snap and release earthquake waves!
fact_bis: Ang mga tectonic plate hinay-hinay nga nagduso hangtod malabwan ang friction, mao nga kalit nga mabali ang bato ug mopagawas og alon sa linog!
evidence: Standing alone, "Plato ug Lindol" reads "Dinner Plate and Earthquake" — the card's own body uses English "tectonic plate" and Cebuano "linog", so both title words are outliers a child cannot bridge.

fact_en: Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air! When it's high, hot days feel super sticky because our sweat evaporates slowly — so we don't cool down as fast!
fact_bis: Ang humidity (kaumog) mao ang gidaghanon sa alisngaw sa tubig sa hangin! Kon taas kini, mas alinsangan ang init tungod kay hinay mosingaw ang singot — maong dili dayon ta mabugnawan!
evidence: "Baul" is a wooden chest/trunk and appears in zero Cebuano bodies for sweat, while this card's body correctly uses "singot", so the headline pairs humidity with furniture.

fact_en: Space is almost a total vacuum — no air to breathe! That's why astronauts wear special suits with oxygen tanks. Sound can't travel in space either, since it needs air to move through!
fact_bis: Ang kawanangan halos vacuum — halos walay hangin nga maginhawa! Mao nga ang mga astronaut magsul-ob og espesyal nga suit ug tangke sa oksiheno. Dili madungog ang tingog kay nagkinahanglan og hangin aron molahos!
evidence: "Kahangturan" is eternity/forever (its only two corpus body uses mean "forever"), whereas outer space is "kawanangan" — the very word this card's body uses — so the headline says "No Air in Eternity".

fact_en: Mayon Volcano mostly erupts andesite! This dark, fine-grained igneous rock is super common in the Bicol Region.
fact_bis: Ang Bulkang Mayon kasagaran nagpagawas og andesite! Kini usa ka ngitngit, pinong igneous rock nga sagad makita sa Bicol Region.
evidence: Last word "Igneo" is cut off; the card itself contains "Igneous".

fact_en: Unlike fair-weather clouds, cumulonimbus clouds produce heavy rain because their water droplets and ice crystals grow too massive to float!
fact_bis: Dili sama sa fair-weather clouds, ang cumulonimbus clouds nag-himo ug kusog nga ulan kay ang water droplets ug ice crystals niini nag-dako kaayo!
evidence: Last word "Cumulonimbu" is cut off; the card itself contains "Cumulonimbus".

fact_en:
Do tectonic plates float on liquid magma?

Tectonic plates do not float on liquid magma, but move over the solid yet plastically flowing rock layer called the asthenosphere!
fact_bis:
Molutaw ba ang mga tectonic plate sa likidong magma?

Ang mga tectonic plate dili molutaw sa likidong magma, pero molihok ibabaw sa solidong bato nga plastiko nga nag-flow, nga gitawag og asthenosphere!
evidence: "Plato" is the everyday Cebuano word for a dinner plate and this card's body says "tectonic plate" in English, so "Asthenosphere Plato" hands the child a dish sitting on the asthenosphere.

fact_en:
What parts of an animal fossilize best?

Hard parts like bones, teeth, and shells fossilize most often! Soft parts like flesh and skin decay quickly and are rarely preserved.
fact_bis:
Unsa nga bahin sa hayop ang pinaka-dali ma-fossil?

Ang gahi nga bahin sama sa bukog, ngipon, ug kabhang ang mas kanunay ma-fossil! Ang humok sama sa unod ug panit dali madunot.
evidence: Cebuano bone is "bukog" (the body's own word, used in 382 corpus bodies) while "buto" means explode/seed, and "Ugipin" is a mashed Tagalog "ug ipin" where "ug ngipon" belongs, making the headline partly a non-word.
